findings.claim: The engine's 4-plane EGA compose page is readable from the SETTLED maze-corridor.state at guest-phys 0x3ffc0 (page segment 0x3ffc), and its viewport decode (uniform 40 B/row, plane stride 0x2000, the offset-preserving page->screen map) is 100.000% byte-exact vs the committed oracle viewport. The base 0x3ffc0 is STABLE across unserialize runs (re-confirmed). The full-screen decode is only 55.66% because the page does NOT hold the static UI chrome (rows 0..31 banner, 144..199 chrome, x0..71/x248..319 side panels) — only the 3D viewport is composed into the page; the chrome is separate VRAM. So the page IS the full viewport, byte-exact, and is the engine's actual OR-blit output for this PURE-BACKGROUND frame.

findings.claim: The OR-blit placement table (cs:[0x190]) + image-descriptor table (cs:[0x18e]) + the source-segment pointers (cs:[0x149]/cs:[0x14d]) are NOT recoverable from the SETTLED maze-corridor.state on the nightly core. They are caller-populated at OR-blit invocation and not persisted. The resident ega.drv OR-blit code copy (located by the OR-store signature AC 26 0A 05 AA at file 0xb2d, reloc base 0x6a1b0) holds its cs:[0x149]=0x1ded / cs:[0x14d]=0x3ddd / cs:[0x18e]=0xbf3f / cs:[0x190]=0xff7f data words at EXACTLY the RAW (unrelocated) disk-file values — so reading the placement table at (0x1ded<<4)+0xff7f yields garbage records (img=255, segDelta pointing to unmapped segments). CONCLUSIVE: scanning ALL OR-store sig copies in RAM, NONE carries the page-segment fingerprint cs:[0x14d]==0x3ffc (the actual page seg) — so no resident relocated copy exposes the real tables. The page seg is set into es by the caller, not via the in-image cs:[0x14d].

evidence.details: ndisasm of ega.drv 0xaa9..0xb40 confirms the walk reads add ax,[cs:0x190] (placement), [cs:0x14d]->es (page seg), [cs:0x149]->ds (src), add ax,[cs:0x18e] (imgdesc). tools/libretro/maze-corridor-scan.ts: 4 sig hits 0x6acdd/0x6acf1/0x6ad08/0x6ad21 = the 4 plane-store loops of ONE code body (deltas 0,0x14,0x2b,0x44 match file plane loops 0xb2d/0xb41/0xb58/0xb71). tools/libretro/maze-corridor-find-tables.ts: for all 13 candidate bases, cs:[0x14d] ∈ {0x3ddd,0x15e5,0x8909,...} — NONE == 0x3ffc (page seg). tools/libretro/maze-corridor-dump-tables.ts: replaying the walk from the raw-derived table gives nonsense placements (segDelta 0x4c0a, srcOff 0x9801, w 152 h 174; src seg reads unmapped at 0xa5ed0).

findings.claim: The from-on-disk-asset background generator is a MULTI-PROBLEM RE effort, not a single remaining deterministic step. Three things are uncracked: (1) the placement/descriptor TABLES are transient (above) — recoverable only by tracing the live OR-blit, which needs the patched core, which CANNOT unserialize the committed gy=121 state (DBPSerialize_CPU divergence -> err unser, re-confirmed across passes); (2) the on-disk floor (id 1346)/ceiling (id 1740)/window assets are wroot asset-DB images loaded via the disk.hdr-keyed asset/decompress loader — that load+decompress path is NOT reversed and there is NO by-id asset decoder in @wiz6/parser (only .pic / wfont / etc.); (3) the asset-block -> 4-plane work-buffer layout mapping the descriptor table indexes into is UNRESOLVED (wmaze-texture-rasterizer.json / maze-floor-ceiling-decoder.json remaining_for_integration). The prior pass's 99.93% same-run pair was captured on the PATCHED core at a DIFFERENT fresh-drive frame (gy=118), not the committed gy=121 state on the nightly. So the task premise 'read the static placement table on the nightly core (the prior pass read it)' does not hold for THIS committed frame — the table is not static and not on the nightly.

The composeBackground walk algorithm itself remains independently gated byte-exact by background.test.ts + the engine 99.93% same-run pair (maze-floor-ceiling-parity.test.ts).
